response.query: What statistical power calculations and assumptions (effect size, variance, alpha, power) justify 150–200/site and 20–50 per failure-mode for detecting clinically meaningful EF/EDV bias?
response.answer: Statistical power calculations assume an effect size of >20% for clinical significance, variance from repeatability testing, and an alpha of 0.05, targeting a power of 80% for 150–200 sites and 20–50 per failure-mode.

results.title: Cardiovascular Disease Risk Tests - Medical Clinical ...
results.content: Aetna considers measurement of apolipoprotein B (apoB) medically necessary for use in high-risk persons with hypercholesterolemia to assess whether additional intense interventions are necessary when LDL cholesterol goals are reached (LDL cholesterol less than 70 mg/dL and non-HDL cholesterol less than 100 mg/dL in persons with known cardio-vascular disease (CVD) or diabetes mellitus, or LDL-C less than 100 mg/dL and non-HDL cholesterol less than 130 mg/dL in persons with other risk factors). Aetna considers noninvasive measurements of arterial elasticity by means of blood pressure waveforms (e.g., CardioVision MS-2000, CVProfilor, Digital Pulse Analyzer (DPA), DSI Pulse Wave Velocity analysis, Max Pulse and HD/PulseWave CR-2000) and noninvasive calculation and analysis of central arterial pressure waveforms (SphygmoCor) experimental, investigational, or unproven for assessing CHD risk because their effectiveness has not been established. Aetna considers cardiac stress testing and stress echocardiography experimental, investigational, or unproven for cardiovascular disease risk assessment in asymptomatic low risk individuals. | I25.10 | Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris [with 2 or more CVD risk factors - see criteria] |
